headline: November scrap looks up $20–$30 a gross ton
detail: Most Steel Market Update sources expect that rise, and one buyer is already offering $30 over October. Mills in eastern Ohio and western Pennsylvania are short, while dealers are holding off until the settle is clear.

headline: Copper hits a 2½-month low as LME stocks climb
detail: LME copper touched $13,883 Tuesday and stocks reached a four-month high of 309,650 tons, while COMEX closed near $6.38, down 2.5%. Yards will likely mark copper down if this holds.

headline: Democrats take both houses of Congress
detail: Divided government likely means less new spending, and traders expect more oversight of AI and data centers. Nasdaq futures fell as much as 2.4% before steadying, and data centers are a big part of the copper demand story.

headline: Gold jumps back over $4,000 after the election
detail: Kitco had gold at about $4,041 early Wednesday, up $112, and silver rose too, as the dollar and Treasury yields fell. Tuesday’s close was $3,929.

headline: Sheet steel posts its biggest weekly jump since March 2025
detail: Spot supply is thin and mills with open tons are charging up, and buyers now expect the tightness to last into 2027. CME Midwest hot-rolled closed at $1,438, up $4.

headline: US mills ran at 88.9% last week, up sharply
detail: Raw steel output jumped 15.7% in a week to 2.053 million tons. Busier mills need more scrap heading into the November settle.

headline: China’s copper premium holds near $200 a ton
detail: The Yangshan import premium stayed at its highest in more than a decade, a sign physical buyers there are still short. It is the main thing limiting the selloff.

headline: US job openings and factory orders beat forecasts
detail: Openings hit 7.52 million and September factory orders rose 1.8%, lifting the 10-year yield near 4.97% before the election. Markets put a December Fed hike at about 79%, which is a headwind for metals.

headline: Factory index hits 55.5, a 10th straight month of growth
detail: The ISM manufacturing reading rose a point in October. Strong factories support metal demand but also keep the Fed leaning toward a hike.

headline: Oil whipsaws on US-Iran deal reports
detail: WTI briefly fell to $93.59 on a report of a near deal, then recovered to about $96.93 after Iran denied it. Oil is driving smelter costs and Fed hike bets right now.

headline: Indonesia hints at deeper nickel ore cuts in 2027
detail: An energy ministry official said next year’s quota cuts may go further than 2026’s, citing a global surplus of about 800,000 tons. That could put a floor under nickel, and stainless scrap with it.

headline: Palladium closes near $936, lowest since June 2025
detail: It fell about 3% Tuesday and is down roughly 20% in a month on fund selling and weak auto demand, before bouncing overnight. Lower palladium means lower catalytic converter payouts.

headline: Platinum closes near $1,418, around a one-year low
detail: Fund outflows and rate-hike bets keep pressure on, and rhodium quotes have not moved. Converter values are leaning on the other two metals.

headline: China central bank move weakens the yuan
detail: The central bank raised the foreign currency reserve requirement and the yuan weakened. That makes dollar-priced metals dearer for Chinese buyers.

headline: China services growth slows to 50.8
detail: The private October survey fell from 51.6 as price cuts met rising costs. It adds to signs of a cooling economy, which weighs on metal demand.

headline: Lutnick is restarting Canada tariff talks
detail: Earlier progress covered lower steel duties under a quota and lower aluminum duties, while autos remain the hard part. A deal could cool US steel and aluminum premiums.

headline: Chile cuts its 2026 copper forecast by 8.4%
detail: Cochilco now sees 4.94 million tons this year and only a small rebound in 2027. That is a floor under copper during the tech selloff.

headline: Congo seizes copper and cobalt in illegal mining crackdown
detail: Authorities took thousands of tons of metal and more than 500 trucks in the mining south. It could tighten informal supply from the world’s No. 2 copper producer.

headline: USW and U.S. Steel still far apart on a contract
detail: The sides are divided on wages and more, over two months past the deadline. A strike at Gary or other mills would hit scrap demand.

headline: Iron ore slips to $91 as Dalian falls
detail: The benchmark lost $0.22 and all 12 brands MMI tracks fell, with Dalian at 671 yuan. Support looks fragile until Chinese mills restock.

headline: Turkish scrap keeps rising
detail: Kallanish says import prices are extending last week’s rebound as suppliers lift their targets, with its index up 0.5%. Firmer export demand helps support US scrap.

headline: Copper scrap estimates slip with COMEX
detail: Metalcharts’ estimates tied to $6.31 copper put bare bright at $4.92–$5.43 and #1 at $4.67–$5.11. Big Daddy’s and Central’s boards are unchanged from yesterday.

headline: Central banks bought 42% more gold in the third quarter
detail: The World Gold Council counted 321 tons of central bank buying, while total demand slipped 1% and jewelry was the weakest for a third quarter on record. Steady official buying supports the price on dips.

headline: US aluminum premium at a record as Canadian metal goes to Europe
detail: The 50% US tariff on Canadian aluminum has pushed US prices to a record gap over world prices. That keeps US scrap aluminum values supported, unless the Canada talks change it.

headline: Drought cuts an Indonesian nickel plant to 30%
detail: Nickel Industries’ ENC plant dropped from about 50% of capacity until rains expected in December. It gives some support to a market still in surplus.

headline: Data centers keep nonresidential building growing
detail: Nonresidential spending rose 0.6% in September, a sixth straight gain, with data centers up 8.6%. That work uses a lot of copper and steel.

headline: Housing starts fell 5.2% in September
detail: Starts dropped to a 1.22 million pace and single-family permits fell 4%. Weaker home building trims demand for copper wire and pipe, aluminum and steel.

headline: Hyundai sets an October sales record
detail: US sales rose 5% to 73,452 as hybrids grew 20%. It is one early read on a month forecast at a soft 15.7 million pace.

headline: Schaeffler to close five European plants
detail: The parts maker will cut 3,460 jobs as combustion demand weakens and Chinese rivals press on price. Weaker European auto output means less metal demand.

headline: Ford lifts its 2026 metal cost estimate to about $2.5 billion
detail: The increase from about $2 billion cites copper and steel, among other costs. Automakers may push suppliers harder as a result.
